answer: The ivory cipher tablet: a claimant carves a cipher into an ivory tablet naming a tide-locked cache on a chosen island, seals it waxed, and buries it at the tide-line marker at low tide. Two island wardens dig it up within three days, decode it against the harbor ledger, and check the grain against the carver's log and the coordinates against the survey register. A wrong cipher, an empty pouch, or a cache claimed twice voids the season, burns a 290-credit stake, and bars the island two seasons. Faking 1,000 identities means carving 1,000 ivory tablets and decoding 1,000 ciphers by hand.
